version.description: Workflow format version. Must be `v1alpha1`; any other value fails the load with rewrite-or-upgrade guidance.

title.description: Picker label. Defaults to the humanized filename, and is truncated to the picker row width.

description.description: Picker subtitle, wrapped or truncated to at most two rows.

hidden.description: Hide from the picker. `hwf run` still launches the workflow.

anyOf.description: Shorthand for a free-form text input with no other settings.
Shorthand for a choice over the configured profile names.
Shorthand for a closed static choice over these values.

type.description: `text` accepts free-form input, `choice` picks from `options:`, `profile` picks from the configured profile names. Inferred as `choice` when `options:` is set, otherwise `text`.

description.description: Shown in the prompt. This is the only part of the prompt line an author controls, so describe every input.

default.description: Pre-filled answer. For a closed `choice` or `profile` it must be one of the available values.

run.description: argv run from the repo root to discover the options, one per line. Elements may template `{{inputs.<earlier>}}` to cascade from an earlier answer; `steps` and `context` roots are load errors. Treat it as read-only. Capped at 10s, 1,000 options, and 8 MiB.

options.description: Values a `choice` offers: a static list, or `{run: argv}` to discover them.

when.description: Guards, in order, that may reference earlier inputs. An inactive input never prompts, resolves, or exports an `HWF_` value, and supplying one fails collection.

allow_custom.description: Accept values outside `options:`, making the list suggestions. `choice` only.

min_length.description: Minimum number of characters for an active answer.

anyOf.description: Full declaration, for a default, a guard, or discovered options.

inputs.description: Values collected before the run, keyed by a name matching `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}`. Only the entry workflow prompts, in declaration order; a child receives values from its parent's step `inputs:`.

anyOf.description: A single template, which becomes the whole result.
Named templates, which become the fields of the result.

returns.description: What a parent's `workflow:` step gets as this workflow's result.

agent.description: Action: prompt text for an agent. Pair with `using:` to start a new agent or `target:` to address a running one. The result is `{response, agent, pane_id}`; the default turn timeout is 30 minutes.

using.description: Profile that starts a new managed agent for this prompt. Mutually exclusive with `target:`; omit both to use the default profile.

target.description: Existing agent name or pane ID to prompt, which must be idle or done. On a step it rejects `pane:`, `cwd:`, and `env:` because the agent already has a pane. Mutually exclusive with `using:`.

run.description: Action: a command. A list is argv with no shell; a string runs through `shell:`. Inputs are exported as `HWF_<name>`. A blocking local run results in `{stdout, stderr, exit_code, failed}`; a placed run results in its readiness payload, and a background run has no result to reference.

shell.description: Shell for a string `run:`, defaulting to `sh`. The argv form rejects it, since argv runs without a shell.

herdr.description: Action: a herdr socket method such as `notification.show`. Nothing is filled in automatically, and a denied method fails at load. The result is the complete herdr payload.

workflow.description: Action: a child workflow, run in isolation. Its `returns:` becomes this step's result; its own `on_failure` does not run under a parent.

inputs.description: Values passed to the child workflow, keyed by its declared input names.

cwd.description: Working directory, defaulting to the invocation working directory. `agent:` and `run:` steps only; `herdr:` and `workflow:` reject it.

env.description: Extra environment variables. `agent:` and `run:` steps only. The `HWF_` prefix is reserved for exported inputs: a `run:` step fails on one at runtime rather than at load, and an agent step passes it through.

open.description: Where the pane goes: a new `tab`, or a `beside`/`below` split of the anchor pane. Accepts a whole-value template when the referenced input is an unconditional closed static choice of those three values.

target.description: Pane to split. `beside`/`below` only; defaults to the invocation pane.

workspace.description: Workspace for the new tab. `tab` only; defaults to the invocation workspace.

size.description: Percent of the anchor given to the new pane. `beside`/`below` only. herdr clamps the effective split ratio, so an extreme value is approximated rather than rejected.

focus.description: Focus the new pane once it opens.

name.description: Name for the created tab, set when the tab opens. `tab` only, because a split joins an existing tab. Template-capable. Defaults to the step ID, which also covers a name that renders blank.

close.description: Close the pane after a successful turn, or after any turn. Foreground `agent:` steps only — a `run:` step and a background step both reject it.

pane.description: Place this step in a herdr pane instead of running it invisibly. `agent:` and `run:` steps only. A placed `run:` must also set `background:` or `ready_when:`, and rejects `pane.close`.

ready_when.description: `/regex/`, no flags, matched against recent pane output to decide the step is ready. `run:` only, and requires both `pane:` and `timeout:`. Matches text already on screen, and does not detect process exit.

timeout.description: Time limit for an `agent:` or `run:` step; `herdr:` and `workflow:` reject it. Omitting it leaves a local `run:` uncapped, but an agent turn still falls back to 30 minutes, and a placed `run:` with `ready_when:` requires it.

one_of.description: Distinct verdict tokens the agent must end its managed response with, on the final non-empty line.

require.description: Subset of `one_of` that lets the step succeed. Omit it to accept every token.

expect.description: Verdict contract for a blocking `agent:` turn. The runner tells the agent to end the managed response with one `one_of` token and to verify it with `hwf response check`, then binds the matched token as `verdict`. A missing, unlisted, or non-`require` verdict fails the step. Rejected on `background:` and on the other three actions.

success_codes.description: Exit codes counted as success instead of the default `[0]`. Blocking local `run:` steps only — a placed, background, or `on_failure` run rejects it, as do the other three actions.

id.description: Not valid on `on_failure`, which runs once and is never guarded.

when.description: Not valid on `on_failure`, which runs once and is never guarded.

continue_on_error.description: Not valid on `on_failure`, which runs once and is never guarded.

background.description: Not valid on `on_failure`, which runs once and is never guarded.

retry.description: Not valid on `on_failure`, which runs once and is never guarded.

on_failure.description: Recovery action, run once after the first non-tolerated failure. Entry workflow only, and `{{context.error}}` is available. Rejects `id`, `when`, `continue_on_error`, `background`, `retry`, and `success_codes`. Skipped entirely when herdr coordination is lost.

id.description: Name this step so later steps can read `{{steps.<id>.field}}` from its result.

when.description: Guard: one clause, or an ordered list evaluated as a short-circuit AND. A clause is a truthiness check or an `==`/`!=` comparison against a quoted string. A false result skips the step.

continue_on_error.description: Tolerate an ordinary failure here: later steps continue and `on_failure` is suppressed, though the run still exits nonzero. A hard failure — a timeout, a capture overflow, or a spawn error — aborts anyway, and lost herdr coordination aborts before this is consulted.

attempts.description: Total attempts including the first, so at least 2.

retry.description: Retry a failed attempt. `run:` and `herdr:` steps only, and never on a background step or in `on_failure`.

steps.description: Steps in execution order. Each uses exactly one of `agent:`, `run:`, `herdr:`, or `workflow:`.

title: herdr-workflows workflow
description: Linear YAML workflow for the herdr-workflows herdr plugin (format v1alpha1). Cross-field rules are enforced by the parser and loader, not this schema.
